html:
Moulay Ismail was the second sultan of the Alaouite dynasty and ruled Morocco from 1672 to 1727, one of the longest reigns of any monarch. He made the dynasty that still rules secure.

He built a vast imperial city at Meknes, with walls, gates, granaries and stables, using forced labour including European captives of the corsairs. His army was the Black Guard, tens of thousands of soldiers of slave origin, loyal only to him.

He took back ports held by Europeans, including Tangier from the English in 1684. He traded letters and embassies with Louis XIV of France. His rule was famous for cruelty, and after his death his sons fought for decades. See also Morocco.
